locator.text: Equation (9.19), p. 113, in the proof of Lemma 9.8

evidence: paper: \begin{array}{l|l} \text{radial physical derivative} & 1/2 + h\kappa_s \\ \text{axial physical derivative} & D = 1/2 - h \\ \text{time physical derivative} & 1 + h \\ \text{derivative of the cylindrical frame} & 1/2. \end{array} \tag{9.19}

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. Three of the four printed rows are in the repository literally, each as a separate item rather than as one table. Row 3 (time, 1+h) is `native_time_power_le` verbatim. Row 2 is `CoordinateAlgebra.D h = 1/2 - h`, and it is used exactly as the axial entry `Q ^ (-D h)` of `chartLinear`. Row 1 is split: `native_radial_power_le` gives the `hκ` part (`radialCoefficient ≤ Q ^ (-h*kappa)`, with `ChartScales.kappa = 1/100000`, the paper's κ_s = 10^-5 of p.105), and `norm_scaledRadial_le` gives the `1/2` part; the `have hpow` step inside `nativeGraph_positive_jet_bound` combines them into `Q ^ (-h*kappa - k/2)`, which is at least as sharp as the printed `k(1/2 + hκ_s)` for k ≥ 1. Row 4 (cylindrical frame, 1/2) is not charged as 1/2 anywhere I found: `rotation_jets` bounds every jet of the frame by a constant in the normalized lift coordinate, and the Q^(-1/2) would come from the Cartesian entries of `chartLinear`. What the repository actually propagates downstream is not the per-direction table but the single worst row: `physicalLift_positive_jet_bound` charges Q^(-k(1+h)) for every derivative of any direction, and everything after it (SharpCommonGraphJets, SharpPhysicalPhase, SharpPhysicalCarrier) uses that uniform cost. Q here is ≤ 1 (`ChartScales.Q_le_one`), so a negative exponent is a loss, as in the paper.
